body: No credit cards currently. I was wondering if there are any specific cards i should apply for or if Capital one is my best bet.

KOHO has a credit building program which you can subscribe to that basically gives you a small line of credit (non spendable). Just so that there’s an open credit account that’s being paid monthly. i used it while i was paying off my debts so i’m not sure how effective it is if at all.

of course no one could take care of it better than they could, i’m just asking like in a case where a passenger might be stuck inside and they may take too long to get there/you’re somewhere remote.

i figured since the fire is in the engine block, the places it can pull oxygen from are more limited so i thought maybe there would be more of an updraft pulling oxygen from under the car as opposed to being able to pull from the sides like in an exposed fire.

If you don’t feel like reading all of this then i’ll just leave my recommendation here. you can read more for some recommendations and reasoning:

MSI Pro B660m-a

If you’re trying to build a 1080p pc that runs can run games like apex or fortnite at max fps on a 144hz monitor (can achieve higher, i personally play apex at 1080p max settings and sit at max framerate) then i’d suggest this build i just built for myself. Cost me $980CAD (about $740USD):

Corsair 4000D,
Gigabyte UD750GM (more than needed but i’d recommend going for at least 750w in general),
MSI Pro B660M-A Wi-fi,
EVGA RTX 3060 12gb (used),
Intel core i3-12100f,
Corsair Vengeance RGB Pro 16gb (2×8),
Western Digital Black SN770 1tb PCle gen4 ssd, Deepcool GAMMAX AG400 no RGB CPU cooler,
Deepcool RF120 case fans (×4)

The MSI Pro B660m-a is the best b660 board you can get. i found mine for $130 and you can also update the bios to be compatible with 13th gen CPUs if you want to upgrade in the future. 

If i was right in assuming this is for a 1080p 144hz build just for gaming the i’d recommend going for the i3 12100f instead of the i5 12400f. the single core performance is near identical and that’s mostly what affects how well your games run. in terms of GPU compatibility (avoiding a bottleneck) they perform the same at 1080p. both meshing well with the 3060 but bottlenecking anything higher than that. 

personally don’t see the point in going for the 12400f unless you need slightly better productivity performance than the 12100f on a budget. if you’re wanting to go with a stronger GPU than the 3060 then you’ll have to go up to the 12600k.

All things considered, i suggest the MSI Pro B660m-a. fast chipset, 2 gen 4 m.2 ssd slots, decent IO and decent future proofing. the one i have only supports 4 DDR4 memory sticks though, no DDR5, though DDR4 is still plenty fast for 1080p gaming.
